narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

instructor.persona: A community elder or a trained lead performer from the region.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Ayyalah originated as a Bedouin war dance performed after tribal victories.
It historically served as a ritual for tribal unity when groups were threatened by enemies.
In 2014, it was recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
on_screen: Map: Oman/UAE · Middle East
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed for weddings, national holidays, state visits, and football matches.
It signifies tribal solidarity, victory, and the protection of the community.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves two rows of men facing each other.
Participants carry bamboo sticks, swords, or rifles.
They move their heads and sticks synchronously with the drum rhythm while hopping from one foot to another.
Watch for Naash, stick movement.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (k8DfMKNWBCE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Two rows of dancers facing each other.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music features large and small drums, tambourines, brass cymbals, leather bagpipes, and flutes.
The melody consists of seven tones in an irregular repeated pattern.
Listen for the large drums, small drums, tambourines, brass cymbals.
A percussive, rhythmic soundscape driven by drums and cymbals, layered with melodic flute or bagpipe lines and communal chanting.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The lead performer is typically an inherited role responsible for training other dancers.
Variants include the Razfah, Al-Harbiyya, Al-Wahabbiyya, and the Ardah.
The dance descends from Bedouin tribal war traditions and pearl diving celebrations.
